title: Meeting Billie Holiday at the Village Vanguard
summary: Heywood introduced them; Billie said she had never noticed a bass until she heard him, and she claimed him after work.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: So one night we were playing and he came up and he said, he stuttered you know, he said Jh - Jh - Jh - John to meet you. I say okay. So I laid my bass down. Went back to the back bar, Billie Holiday is standing there. I didn't recognize her, in fact I don't recall having seen her picture, but I heard her records out here before I ever left here. The first record I recall having heard her sing was "Sun Bonnet Blue and the Yellow Straw Hat." And he says "John Simmons, Billie Holiday," I say Wow! I say I sure have admired your work down through the years before I ever become a musician, I admired your work. She say oh man, she laughed and said give him a drink. So I had a brandy alexander. We stood there and talked. Eddie came back and say all right let's go back. She say you all go back I'm talking to John. So we stood there and talked.

She say, you know, I never noticed a bass before, she said "I never heard a bass before," she said I-she just took it for granted that that was something that was supposed to be in the band. She said "I've had a whole lot of bass players and I never heard any of them, but she said "I heard you." She said "to-
night when you get off, why don't you come by the Three Deuces to pick me up. I say what time you get off, she say oh I get off around about three but I'll wait until you come. I say okay.

So I went after her. I'm walking in. She's walking out with company. She bowed her head. I say that's all right, some other time, you know. So I knew some of the musicians on the street anyway. So I hung out with them. Went around the corner, got the last drink before they closed up.
And the next night, I'm down in the Village Vanguard, she showed up down there and collected me.

Yeah. She was there when I got off. She claimed me. I say wow! Ain't this something! Here's someone I've admired for years, has turned out like this. I've got to go for her. Wow! I'm not going to be no Mr. Holiday, I'm still going to maintain myself, you know. My dignity. I'm John Simmons, I mean I'm not as great a bass player as she is a singer, but I still want to be known as John Simmons, the bassist. Not John Simmons, Lady Day's man, you know. So she worked across Onyx the street at the Mike (E) [Osserman] Club for... Osserman, I think, was his last name. And I was over here across the street with Sammy Kaye and Alexander. What is his first name? I can't think of his first name.
